translationRepairs: Huang Gan, whose courtesy name was Zhizhi, came from Min County in Fuzhou.
Huang Gan, whose courtesy name was Zhiqing, came from Min County in Fuzhou.
字直卿 gives courtesy name Zhiqing (直+卿); idiomatic Zhizhi misreads 卿 and invents a wrong name.
Huang Gan, courtesy name Zhizhi, was a native of Min County in Fuzhou.
Huang Gan, courtesy name Zhiqing, was a native of Min County in Fuzhou.
Same 字直卿; literal Zhizhi is the same courtesy-name error and Zhiqing restores the graphs.
Xi told others, "Zhizhi's resolve is iron and his thought relentless; company with him does one real good."
Xi told others, "Zhiqing's resolve is iron and his thought relentless; company with him does one real good."
Zhu Xi's quote names 直卿; English Zhizhi mismatches that courtesy name, and Zhiqing matches 直卿.
Xi told others, "Zhizhi's will is firm and his thinking arduous; to be with him is of great benefit."
Xi told others, "Zhiqing's will is firm and his thinking arduous; to be with him is of great benefit."
Quoted 直卿 in the same speech; literal Zhizhi is wrong and Zhiqing is the correct romanization.
When Xi completed the Bamboo Grove Retreat he wrote Gan a letter saying, "When the time comes you may ask Zhizhi to step directly into my chair."
When Xi completed the Bamboo Grove Retreat he wrote Gan a letter saying, "When the time comes you may ask Zhiqing to step directly into my chair."
Letter wording 請直卿代即講席 uses 直卿; idiomatic Zhizhi invents the wrong courtesy name.
When Xi finished the Bamboo Grove Retreat, he sent Gan a letter with the words, "When the time comes you may ask Zhizhi to take my place at the lecture seat."
When Xi finished the Bamboo Grove Retreat, he sent Gan a letter with the words, "When the time comes you may ask Zhiqing to take my place at the lecture seat."
Same letter quote 直卿; literal Zhizhi is incorrect and Zhiqing restores it.

Lie, who deeply respected Gan's name and virtue, appointed him to the Jing-Shang wine depot of the Hubei pacification commission with additional preparatory dispatch; whenever anything was amiss he offered loyal remonstrance and fought it through.

Lie, who deeply respected Gan's name and virtue, appointed him to the reward wine depot of the Jinghu North Circuit pacification commission with additional preparatory dispatch; whenever anything was amiss he offered loyal remonstrance and fought it through.
荊湖北路安撫司激賞酒庫 is the Jinghu North Circuit pacification commission's reward wine depot; Jing-Shang and bare Hubei invent a place-name and drop the circuit designation.

Lie, who greatly respected Gan's reputation and virtue, appointed him to the Jing-Shang wine depot of the Hubei pacification commission with additional duty as preparatory dispatch; whenever policy was wrong he would offer loyal remonstrance and strive to the utmost.

Lie, who greatly respected Gan's reputation and virtue, appointed him to the reward wine depot of the Jinghu North Circuit pacification commission with additional duty as preparatory dispatch; whenever policy was wrong he would offer loyal remonstrance and strive to the utmost.
Same office title 激賞酒庫 under 荊湖北路; literal Jing-Shang/Hubei repeats the mistranslation.
At Hanyang he built halls on Phoenix Perch Hill behind the yamen to lodge scholars from afar and raised shrines to Zhou, the Cheng brothers, You, and Zhu.
At Hanyang he built halls on Phoenix Perch Hill behind the yamen to lodge scholars from afar and raised shrines to the four masters Zhou, Cheng, You, and Zhu.
周、程、游、朱四先生 names four masters with singular 程; Cheng brothers invents a fifth referent against 四先生.

I thought when the ruler returned he would bitterly blame himself, lodge outside the palace, and greatly warn the realm, saying, "This is my fault; whoever can admonish my errors, enter quickly and remonstrate."

I thought when you returned with your entourage you would bitterly blame yourself, lodge outside, and greatly warn the realm, saying, "This is my fault; whoever can admonish my errors, enter quickly and remonstrate."
切意千乘言旋 addresses the addressee's return with a commander's entourage, not a ruler returning to a palace; you/entourage and lodge outside restore that sense.
Ordered to Chaozhou he declined; assigned to Mingdao Palace in Bozhou, within a month he sought retirement, was granted it, and made Gentlemen for Discussion.
Ordered to Chaozhou he declined; assigned to Mingdao Palace in Bozhou, within a month he sought retirement, was granted it, and made Gentleman for Discussion.
特授承議郎 is one personal rank; Gentlemen wrongly pluralizes the title granted to him alone.

Soon he was ordered to administer Chaozhou; he declined and would not go; he was assigned to oversee Mingdao Palace in Bozhou; after a month he begged retirement; the edict granted it and he was specially made Gentlemen for Discussion.

Soon he was ordered to administer Chaozhou; he declined and would not go; he was assigned to oversee Mingdao Palace in Bozhou; after a month he begged retirement; the edict granted it and he was specially made Gentleman for Discussion.
Same singular 承議郎; Gentleman for Discussion corrects the pluralized rank title.
Years after his death disciples sought a posthumous name; he was given Court Tribute and one son lower-prefecture literary studies; posthumous title Wensu.

Years after his death disciples sought a posthumous name; he was specially granted the rank of Gentleman for Court Service, one son received lower-prefecture literary studies, and his posthumous title was Wensu.
又特贈朝奉郎 is the ranked prestige title Gentleman for Court Service; Court Tribute invents a different honor.

Several years after his death, at his disciples' request for a posthumous title, he was also specially given Recipient of Court Tribute and one son was granted lower-prefecture literary studies; his posthumous title was Wensu.

Several years after his death, at his disciples' request for a posthumous title, he was also specially given the rank of Gentleman for Court Service and one son was granted lower-prefecture literary studies; his posthumous title was Wensu.
Same 朝奉郎; Recipient of Court Tribute is not that rank, and Gentleman for Court Service restores it.
Fan died at seventy; given Direct Huawen Gentleman and posthumous Wendi; his son received lower-prefecture literary studies.
Fan died at seventy; given Direct Huawen Gentleman and posthumous Wending; his son received lower-prefecture literary studies.
諡文定 is posthumous Wending; Wendi misreads 定 as 帝/di.
Fan died at seventy; he was given Direct Gentleman of the Huawen Pavilion and posthumous title Wendi; his son was granted lower-prefecture literary studies.
Fan died at seventy; he was given Direct Gentleman of the Huawen Pavilion and posthumous title Wending; his son was granted lower-prefecture literary studies.
Same 諡文定; literal Wendi is the same error and Wending matches 文定.
When Shi Miyuan ruled and deposed Prince Qi, Fan, seeing the three bonds at stake, never went out again.
When Shi Miyuan ruled and deposed Imperial Son Hong, Fan, seeing the three bonds at stake, never went out again.
廢皇子竑 names Imperial Son Hong (竑); Prince Qi invents an unstated peerage and drops the given name.
At that time Shi Miyuan held the state; he deposed Prince Qi; Fan, because the three bonds were involved, from then on never went out again.
At that time Shi Miyuan held the state; he deposed Imperial Son Hong; Fan, because the three bonds were involved, from then on never went out again.
Same 皇子竑; literal Prince Qi is unsupported and Imperial Son Hong restores title plus given name.
he reported to veteran generals skilled in the arts to lead the lazy and lax.
he engaged veteran generals skilled in the arts to lead the lazy and lax.
稟老將之長於藝者 means engaging skilled veteran generals; reported to invents a wrong agent relation.

Thinking he could not repay the state in retirement, Fan recommended Cui Yuzhi, Wei Liaoweng, Zhen Dexiu, Chen Mi, Zheng Yin, Yang Changru, Ding Fu, Qi Zai, Gong Weifan, Xu Qiao, Liu Zai, and Hong Ziakui.

Thinking he could not repay the state in retirement, Fan recommended Cui Yuzhi, Wei Liaoweng, Zhen Dexiu, Chen Mi, Zheng Yin, Yang Changru, Ding Fu, Qi Zai, Gong Weifan, Xu Qiao, Liu Zai, and Hong Zikui.
洪咨夔 romanizes as Hong Zikui (咨 zī + 夔 kuí); Ziakui is a misspelling of the given name.

Zhen Dexiu and the right historiographer Wei Liaoweng recommended him; he was given acting vice-prefect of Longxing Prefecture; Jiangxi commander Wei Dayou appointed him consulting officer—all declined—and he was finally made direct gentleman of the Secretariat in charge of Zhidao Palace in Qingyuan.

Zhen Dexiu and the right historiographer Wei Liaoweng recommended him; he was given acting vice-prefect of Longxing Prefecture; Jiangxi commander Wei Dayou appointed him consulting officer—all declined—and he was finally made direct gentleman of the Secretariat supervising Qingyuan Zhidao Palace.

主管慶元至道宮 is a Qingyuan Zhidao Palace sinecure title, not residence at a palace in Qingyuan; the proposed parenthetical is awkward, so keep Qingyuan as part of the office name without locating him there.
When community granaries were enacted Qia borrowed three hundred piculs of ever-normal grain, built a village granary, returned principal in six years, and villagers profited.

When the community-granary law was in force, Qia asked the county to lend three hundred piculs of ever-normal grain, built a granary in the village, returned the principal in six years, and the villagers profited.
洽請於縣，貸常平米 states he asked the county to lend grain; idiomatic borrowed omits that petition.

His friends were famous men—Lü Zujian, Huang Gan, Zhao Chongxian, Cai Yuan, Wu Bida, Fu Guang, Li Daochuan, Li Fan, Ye Weidao, Li Hongzu, Li Fangzi, Chai Zhongxing, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Li Qi, Zhao Rujing, Chen Guiyi, Du Xiaoyan, Du Zheng, Zhang Sigu—all revered him.

His friends were famous men—Lü Zujian, Huang Gan, Zhao Chongxian, Cai Yuan, Wu Bida, Fu Guang, Li Daochuan, Li Fan, Ye Weidao, Li Hongzu, Li Fangzi, Chai Zhongxing, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Li Zhi, Zhao Rujing, Chen Guiyi, Du Xiaoyan, Du Zheng, Zhang Sigu—all revered him.
李埴 has given name 埴 (zhí); Li Qi misreads the character and Li Zhi restores it.
Before long Shu's bandits in Nan'an were about to invade the border; hearing there were preparations, they withdrew.
Before long the Shu bandits of Nan'an were about to invade the border; hearing there were preparations, they withdrew.
南安舒寇 names Shu bandits tied to Nan'an; Shu's bandits over-reads 舒 as a possessive polity genitive.
the sage's ground of great completion has thousands of joints and ten thousand eyes—how much effort is that.
the sage's ground of great completion has thousands of joints and myriad items—how much effort is that.
千節萬目 uses 目 for items/points of detail; ten thousand eyes is a false literalization.
In the ninth year of Jiading, awaiting examination in the capital, returning he passed Yanling; Prefect Zheng Zhitie led staff to extend him at the prefectural school.
In the ninth year of Jiading, awaiting examination in the capital, returning he passed Yanling; Prefect Zheng Zhitie led his staff to invite him to lecture at the prefectural school.
率僚屬延講郡庠 means led staff to invite him to lecture; extend him obscures 延講.
Someone told Miyuan, "This is truly Zhen Dexiu's faction."
Someone told Miyuan, "This is Zhen Dexiu's faction."
此真德秀黨也 uses 真 as the surname in 真德秀; truly invents an adverb from that graph.
Guangzong made him Imperial Sacrifices recorder; he said ritual teaching was abandoned and asked offices to revise Zhenghe rites and books by Sima Guang and Gao Min and enact them.
Guangzong made him Imperial Sacrifices recorder; he said ritual teaching was abandoned and asked offices to revise Zhenghe rites and books by Sima Guang and Gao Kang and enact them.
高閌 is Gao Kang (閌 kāng); Gao Min misreads the given-name graph.

When Emperor Guangzong took the throne he was moved to recorder of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized that ritual teaching was now abandoned and asked the relevant offices to take the Zhenghe crown, wedding, mourning, and burial rites and books by Sima Guang, Gao Min, and others, revise and enact them.

When Emperor Guangzong took the throne he was moved to recorder of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized that ritual teaching was now abandoned and asked the relevant offices to take the Zhenghe crown, wedding, mourning, and burial rites and books by Sima Guang, Gao Kang, and others, revise and enact them.
Same 高閌; literal Gao Min is wrong and Gao Kang restores the name.

When Zhu Xi administered Nan'kang, Hao performed the disciple's rites, questioning and raising difficult points.
質疑問難 means posing difficult questions, so seeking difficulty is wrong; keep Nan'kang to avoid a merely stylistic place-name change bundled with that fix.
